$comment: Canonical JSON vectors per spec/06-conformance.md#canonical-json. Every runtime's canonicalization routine must produce `expected` exactly, byte-for-byte, from `input`. `input` is given as parsed JSON for readability; a runtime's serializer output is what's being tested, not its parser. Array element order is never sorted; only object keys are. Money integers must render as bare integers; timestamps must render as fixed-precision UTC with a literal Z.

cases.description: flat object, keys out of order
nested objects, keys sorted at every level independently
deeply nested object, keys sorted at every level
array element order is preserved, never sorted
array of objects: element order preserved, each object's own keys sorted
Money minor_units must render as a bare integer, never a float, even at a round major-unit value
cases.why: 10000 minor units is exactly 100.00 ETB; a serializer that 'helpfully' normalizes a round integer to a float representation (10000.0) or scientific notation (1e4) violates Invariant I1 at the serialization layer even though the underlying value was correctly an integer. See spec/02-invariants.md#i1.

cases.description: negative Money value renders with a leading minus and no other change
zero Money value renders as bare 0, not 0.0
large integer within int64 range renders in full, never in exponential notation
timestamp is ISO-8601 UTC, second precision, literal Z offset
cases.why: Never fractional seconds (2026-01-15T09:30:00.000Z) and never a +00:00 offset form; both are logically equivalent but not byte-identical, which is the only bar that matters here. See spec/06-conformance.md.

cases.description: no insignificant whitespace anywhere, including around the empty object and empty array
string values use standard JSON escaping; forward slash is not escaped and non-ASCII is emitted as UTF-8, not \u-escaped
object keys are sorted byte-wise even when one key is non-ASCII: the multi-byte UTF-8 encoding of an Amharic key numerically follows every ASCII key, so it sorts last
two non-ASCII keys are still sorted byte-wise relative to each other, not merely grouped after ASCII keys
control characters, quotes, and backslashes inside a string value are all escaped per standard JSON string escaping, regardless of the no-HTML-escaping rule for characters like < and &
an empty object and an empty array nested two levels deep, each rendered with no whitespace
an empty array and an empty object as sibling top-level values, key order still governed purely by the key names, not by which value is empty
a null value at the top level of a field (e.g. PaymentResult.next_action for a terminal status) renders as bare null, not omitted and not the string "null"
boolean values render as bare true/false, never quoted
a negative integer at the int64 boundary renders in full, matching the corresponding vectors/money/conversions.json int64-boundary case, never in exponential notation
